subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of these is a manufactured board rather than a natural timber?
questions.explain: MDF is a manufactured board made from compressed wood fibres and resin, whereas oak, pine and mahogany are natural timbers.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes hardwoods from softwoods?
options: Hardwoods come from coniferous trees, softwoods from deciduous trees
Hardwoods come from deciduous (broad-leaved) trees, softwoods from coniferous trees
Hardwoods are always physically harder than softwoods
questions.explain: The hardwood/softwood classification is botanical: hardwoods come from broad-leaved deciduous trees and softwoods from coniferous (cone-bearing) trees, regardless of actual hardness.

questions.q: Which property describes a material's ability to be drawn out into a thin wire?
questions.explain: Ductility is the ability of a material to be stretched or drawn into a wire without breaking, a property seen in copper.

questions.q: Which of these is a thermochromic (smart) material?
options: An alloy that returns to a remembered shape when heated
A board made from recycled paper
A pigment that changes colour with temperature
questions.explain: Thermochromic materials change colour in response to temperature changes, used in items like mood rings and battery testers.

questions.q: When selecting a material for a children's outdoor playground slide, the most important property is:
options: Durability and weather resistance with a smooth, non-toxic finish
questions.explain: An outdoor slide must withstand weather and repeated use safely, so durability, weather resistance and a smooth non-toxic surface are the priority.

questions.q: A non-ferrous metal is best described as one that:
options: Is always an alloy of two metals
Contains no iron and does not rust
Is harder than any ferrous metal
questions.explain: Non-ferrous metals such as aluminium and copper contain no iron, so they are generally not magnetic and do not rust.

questions.q: A shape-memory alloy such as Nitinol is useful because it:
options: Returns to a pre-set shape when heated
Glows in the dark after exposure to light
questions.explain: Shape-memory alloys can be deformed and then return to their original 'remembered' shape when heated above a transition temperature.

questions.q: Which is a natural fibre rather than a synthetic one?
questions.explain: Cotton is a natural fibre grown from the cotton plant, whereas polyester, nylon and acrylic are synthetic fibres made from polymers.

questions.q: Malleability is the property that allows a material to be:
options: Hammered or rolled into thin sheets without cracking
Returned to its original shape after a force is removed
questions.explain: Malleability is the ability of a material to be deformed by compression, such as hammering or rolling into sheets, without breaking.

A ferrous metal that rusts easily
questions.explain: Brass is an alloy made by combining copper and zinc, giving it good corrosion resistance and machinability.

questions.q: Plywood is made stronger and more stable than solid timber by:
options: Gluing thin veneers with the grain of each layer at right angles to the next
Adding only metal to the surface
questions.explain: Plywood is built from layers of veneer bonded with the grain of each layer running at right angles, which resists warping and adds strength in both directions.

questions.q: Carbon-fibre reinforced polymer is an example of a composite because it:
options: Can be melted and remoulded endlessly
Combines two or more materials to gain improved properties
questions.explain: A composite combines two or more different materials, such as carbon fibres in a resin matrix, to achieve a high strength-to-weight ratio.
